title: Preterite vs Imperfect
description: Master the difference between preterite (past completed) and imperfect (past ongoing/habitual) tenses in Spanish.

grammar.title: Preterite — Completed Past Actions
grammar.content:
PRETERITE TENSE (Pretérito Indefinido) — for completed actions in the past:

Use for:
1. A completed action with a clear beginning and end
2. Actions that happened once
3. A series of completed actions
4. Specific dates or times in the past

Regular forms:
Hablar → hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron
Comer → comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron
Vivir → viví, viviste, vivió, vivimos, vivisteis, vivieron

Irregular preterites:
Ser/Ir → fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron
Tener → tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron
Hacer → hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron
Poder → pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudisteis, pudieron
Querer → quise, quisiste, quiso, quisimos, quisisteis, quisieron
Venir → vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron
examples: Ayer compre un libro. (Yesterday I bought a book.)
La semana pasada fui a Madrid. (Last week I went to Madrid.)
Cuando llegue, el ya se habia ido. (When I arrived, he had already left.)

grammar.title: Imperfect — Ongoing/Habitual Past
grammar.content:
IMPERFECT TENSE (Pretérito Imperfecto) — for ongoing or habitual past actions:

Use for:
1. Actions that continued over time
2. Habitual or repeated actions in the past
3. Descriptions in the past
4. Background information
5. Age, time, weather in the past

Regular forms:
Hablar → hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban
Comer → comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían
Vivir → vivía, vivías, vivía, vivíamos, vivíais, vivían

Key 'to be' verbs in imperfect:
Ser → era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran
Ir → iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban
Ver → veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían

Descriptions:
Era un dia hermoso. (It was a beautiful day.)
Llovía mucho. (It was raining a lot.)
Tenía 10 años. (I was 10 years old.)
examples: Cuando era niño, vivía en el campo. (When I was a child, I lived in the countryside.)
Cada día iba a la escuela. (Every day I went to school.)
El cielo estaba gris. (The sky was gray.)
Llovía y hacía frío. (It was raining and it was cold.)

grammar.title: Preterite vs Imperfect — When to Use Each
grammar.content:
Key decision tree:

1. Was the action COMPLETED or ONGOING?
   - Completed → preterite
   - Ongoing/habitual → imperfect

2. Tell me what happened vs. What was happening?
   - 'What happened' → preterite
   - 'What was happening' → imperfect

Common cases:

Preterite:
- Ayer compre (yesterday I bought)
- Nací en 1990 (I was born in 1990)
- Llegó a las 8 (he arrived at 8)
- Dejó de fumar (he stopped smoking)

Imperfect:
- Cuando era niño (when I was a child)
- Siempre llegaba tarde (he was always late)
- Llovía (it was raining)
- Eran las tres (it was three o'clock)

With 'cuando' (when):
- Cuando llegué, él salió → preterite + preterite (two completed actions)
- Cuando era niño, vivía aquí → imperfect + imperfect (two ongoing actions)

State changes (preterite):
- Me enamoré (I fell in love)
- Se mudó (he moved)
- Murió (he died)

Physical states (imperfect):
- Estaba cansado (I was tired)
- Tenía hambre (I was hungry)
examples: Ayer compre un libro. (Yesterday I bought a book) — completed action
Cuando era niño, leía muchos libros. (When I was a child, I read many books) — habitual
Estaba lloviendo cuando salí. (It was raining when I left) — imperfect + preterite
Dejó de fumar hace dos años. (He stopped smoking two years ago) — completed change

pronunciation.title: Preterite vs Imperfect Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Key pronunciation differences:

Preterite (completed):
- hablé (ah-BLAY) — é stresses the vowel
- comí (koh-MEE) — í stresses the vowel
- vivió (bee-BEE-oh) — í stresses the vowel

Imperfect (ongoing):
- hablaba (ah-blah-BAH) — stress on -ba-
- comía (koh-MEE-ah) — stress on -mí-
- vivía (bee-BEE-ah) — stress on -ví-

Key difference: Preterite has accented endings (-é, -ió) while imperfect does not (except -ía which is not accented in writing but stressed).

Preterite 3rd person singular (-ó) sounds like 'oh' while imperfect 3rd person singular (-ía) sounds like 'ee-ah'.
examples: hablé = ah-BLAY (I spoke — completed)\nhablaba = ah-blah-BAH (I was speaking — ongoing)
comí = koh-MEE (I ate — completed)\ncomía = koh-MEE-ah (I was eating — ongoing)
vivió = bee-BEE-oh (he lived/died — completed)\nvivía = bee-BEE-ah (he was living — ongoing)

exercises.question: Which is correct: 'When I was a child' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Cuando era niño' uses imperfect 'era' (was) for ongoing state. 'Cuando fui' is preterite (when I became/was). Both can be correct depending on meaning.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ayer ___ al supermercado. (Yesterday I went to the supermarket.)'
exercises.explanation: Fui = I went (preterite of ir). This is a completed action on a specific day (ayer).

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'It was raining' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Llovía = it was raining (imperfect). Describes ongoing action in the past.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Cuando ___ 10 años, vivía en Barcelona. (When I was 10 years old, I lived in Barcelona.)'
exercises.explanation: Tenía = I had/was (imperfect). Describes age in the past. 'Cuando tenía 10 años' = When I was 10 years old.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses preterite correctly?
options: La semana pasada fui a la playa
exercises.explanation: 'La semana pasada fui a la playa' uses preterite 'fui' (I went) for a completed action on a specific past time.

exercises.question: Complete: 'El año pasado ___ en Madrid. (Last year I lived in Madrid.)'
exercises.explanation: Viví = I lived (preterite). A completed period of time in the past.

exercises.question: Which is correct: 'I fell in love' (completed action)?
exercises.explanation: 'Me enamoré' is preterite — a completed state change (fell in love). 'Estaba enamorado' would be imperfect (was in love).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Mientras ___ la televisión, alguien llamó. (While I was watching TV, someone called.)'
exercises.explanation: Veía = I was watching (imperfect). Describes ongoing action interrupted by preterite 'llamó'.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'I was always late' (habitual)?
exercises.explanation: Llegaba = I was arriving (imperfect). Habitual past action described with imperfect.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Dejó de fumar ___ dos años. (He stopped smoking two years ago.)'
exercises.explanation: Hace + time + que + preterite = ago. 'Hace dos años' = two years ago. The action 'dejó' (stopped) is preterite.
